5 scallions or green onions, ends trimmed Salt to taste if desired
ingredients.preparation: ends trimmed Salt to taste if desired

ingredients.raw: 3 tablespoons finely chopped fresh chives or parsley
ingredients.item: finely chopped fresh chives or parsley

steps.text: Cut carrots into 1 ½-inch lengths. Cut each length into slices about ¼ inch thick. Stack slices and cut into ¼-inch-thick strips. There should be about 2 cups.
Slice turnips and cut into strips of approximately the same size.
Cut scallions into 1 ½-inch lengths. There should be about a cup.

Place carrots in saucepan and add cold water to cover with salt to taste. Bring to boil and let simmer about 3 minutes. Add turnips and let simmer about 3 minutes. Add pieces of scallion and continue cooking about 30 seconds.
Drain well. Return vegetables to saucepan and add butter, salt and pepper. Add chives or parsley and toss to blend.

ingredients.raw: 1 red ripe tomato, cored and cut into eighths

steps.text: Trim off the tough stems of the watercress. Core the Boston lettuce and separate leaves. Rinse greens and shake off any excess moisture. Put greens in a mixing bowl and add the tomato.
Blend vinegar, garlic and mustard in a small mixing bowl. Stir with a whisk, gradually adding the oil. Add salt and pepper. Pour over greens and tomato and toss.

name: Mixed Green Salad With Anchovy Sauce
author: Pierre Franey

steps.text: Trim lettuce and cut into fairly large but still bite-size pieces. There should be about 8 cups. Put in a salad bowl.
Trim endive and cut into bite-size pieces. There should be about 4 cups. Add to the bowl.
Put mustard, anchovy paste, garlic, vinegar, salt and pepper in small mixing bowl. Beat with wire whisk while gradually adding oil.
Pour sauce over salad greens and toss to blend.

name: Mixed Green Salad With Blue Cheese Dressing
author: Pierre Franey

ingredients.raw: ½ cup crumbled blue cheese like Roquefort, Saga or Danish blue
Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

ingredients.raw: 10 cups loosely packed bite-size pieces watercress, red-leaf lettuce and Belgian endive

steps.text: Combine the vinegar, garlic, mustard and cheese in a mixing bowl. Blend well. Add the oil, salt and pepper in a small mixing bowl and blend well with a wire whisk.
Place the salad greens in a bowl. Pour the dressing over the greens and toss well.

ingredients.raw: ½ teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
¼ cup pitted green olives, coarsely chopped

steps.text: In a large bowl, toss together the romaine, watercress and radicchio. In another bowl, whisk together the yogurt, olive oil and lime juice. Stir in the salt, pepper and olives. Just before serving, toss the dressing with the salad.

ingredients.raw: 4 ounces mixed green and red lettuce

steps.text: Wash and dry greens.
Whisk oil, vinegar and Worcestershire in serving bowl; stir in lettuce.

name: Mixed Greens and Tomatoes With Raspberry Vinaigrette
author: Marian Burros

ingredients.raw: 2 small tomatoes, if good and ripe; otherwise omit
ingredients.preparation: if good and ripe; otherwise omit

steps.text: Wash the greens; drain and dry. Cut up the tomatoes, if using.
In serving bowl, whisk the oil and vinegar together.
Stir the greens and optional tomatoes into the dressing.

name: Mixed-Greens Pie With Cornmeal Crust
author: Sara Dickerman
description: Sara Dickerman

ingredients.raw: ⅓ cup, plus 3 tablespoons, extra-virgin olive oil
2 large leeks, white and light green parts only, cut into ⅛-inch slices (about 2 cups)
ingredients.preparation: white and light green parts only, cut into ⅛-inch slices (about 2 cups)

ingredients.raw: 1 pound mixed dark greens (chard, lacinato kale, spinach), washed, stems removed and cut into broad ribbons
ingredients.preparation: lacinato kale, spinach), washed, stems removed and cut into broad ribbons

ingredients.raw: 4 scallions, white and light green parts only, thinly sliced
ingredients.preparation: white and light green parts only, thinly sliced

ingredients.raw: 2 ounces kefalograviera, kefaloteri or kasseri cheese, grated (about a heaping ½ cup)
ingredients.preparation: kefaloteri or kasseri cheese, grated (about a heaping ½ cup)

ingredients.raw: ½ cup manouri or feta cheese

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees. Grease a 10-inch straight-sided skillet or baking pan with 2 tablespoons of the olive oil. In a deep-sided sauté pan at least 12 inches wide, heat ⅓ cup olive oil over medium heat. Add the leeks and cook, stirring occasionally, until they have softened but not colored, about 10 minutes. Add as many of the greens as can fit in the pot, along with 1 teaspoon salt. Stir and cover until the greens have wilted, 2 to 3 minutes. Add the remaining greens, stir, and cover until they have wilted, another 2 to 3 minutes. Remove from the heat and stir in the scallions, dill and parsley. Transfer the mixture to a colander set over a bowl and let cool to room temperature.

Meanwhile, in a large bowl, mix the kefalograviera, ricotta and manouri. Squeeze excess liquid from the cooled greens and add them to the cheeses. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Stir in the eggs and set aside.

In a small saucepan, heat the milk over medium heat until it starts to bubble. Whisk in the cornmeal and 1 teaspoon salt. Continue stirring as the mixture thickens into an almost unstirrable paste. Remove from the heat. With lightly floured fingers, press half of the mixture into a thin layer across the bottom of the prepared pan. Top with the greens and cheese filling, spreading each evenly to the edges. Stir about ½ cup water into the remaining cornmeal to make a milkshake-thick batter (there will be a few lumps). Pour the thinned batter across the filling (some greens will poke through). Drizzle the remaining tablespoon of olive oil across the top of the pie. Bake until firm and golden brown around the edges, about 1 hour.
Serve warm or at room temperature, with Greek yogurt on the side.

name: Mixed Greens Salad With Dijon Vinaigrette
author: Pierre Franey

ingredients.raw: Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

ingredients.raw: 10 cups loosely packed bite-size pieces of watercress, red-leaf lettuce and Belgian endive
ingredients.item: loosely packed bite-size pieces of watercress

steps.text: Combine the vinegar, garlic and mustard in a mixing bowl. Blend well.
Add the oil, salt and pepper and blend well with a wire whisk.
Place the onion rings and salad greens in a bowl and toss well with the dressing.

ingredients.raw: Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

ingredients.raw: 2 ripe plum tomatoes, cored and sliced thin
1 medium Vidalia or red onion, peeled and sliced thin
Shaved Gruyere or Parmesan cheese for garnish
ingredients.item: shaved gruyere or parmesan cheese for garnish

steps.text: Core the Boston lettuce and separate the leaves. Trim off the tough stems of the watercress. Rinse the greens well and shake off the excess moisture.
In a large salad bowl, add the mustard, the vinegar and the garlic. Blend well with a wire whisk, gradually adding the oil. Add salt and pepper to taste.
Add the lettuce, watercress, tomatoes and the sliced onion. Toss well and serve with shaved Gruyere or Parmesan cheese on top, or with a wedge of Brie on the side.

ingredients.raw: 1 pound sea bass fillets or fillets of other white-fleshed fish, skin on or off as you wish
ingredients.item: sea bass fillets or fillets of other white-fleshed fish
ingredients.preparation: skin on or off as you wish

steps.text: Cut the fish fillets crosswise into portions approximately 4 ounces. Salt them and set aside.
Shell and devein shrimp. Leave tails attached.
Cut chicken into 1-inch or slightly larger pieces and score each a few times.
Clean mushrooms and slice. Reserve stems for use in stocks or soups.
Preheat oven to 475 degrees or, if cooking over coals, make sure they are red hot with no flame.

Butter the centers of four 12-inch squares of aluminum foil. In the center of each square, place a portion of fish fillet. On top and around it arrange shrimp, chicken and mushroom slices. Top with a pat of butter and a lemon slice. Sprinkle the sake evenly over each portion. Fold up into packets and crimp edges so each packet is tightly sealed.
Place packets on grill above coals and grill for 10 minutes. Do not turn. If using oven, bake for 15 to 20 minutes. Serve hot on individual plates with light soy sauce.

name: Mixed Mushroom And Sweet Potato Stuffing
author: Amanda Hesser

ingredients.raw: 4 medium sweet potatoes or yams, peeled and in large dice (4 cups)
ingredients.preparation: peeled and in large dice (4 cups)

ingredients.raw: 1 pound mixed wild mushrooms (shiitake, portobello or cremini) (4 cups), cleaned, stemmed and in large dice
ingredients.preparation: portobello or cremini) (4 cups), cleaned, stemmed and in large dice

ingredients.raw: 1 small red onion, finely chopped (1 cup)
2 sprigs thyme, plus 1 tablespoon minced thyme
8 cups day-old sourdough bread, in large dice (one 2-pound round loaf, trimmed of crust)
ingredients.preparation: in large dice (one 2-pound round loaf, trimmed of crust)

steps.text: Adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 350 degrees. In roasting pan, place sweet potatoes, olive oil and 1 tablespoon sage leaves , sprinkle with salt and pepper and toss to combine. Roast until golden brown and tender, tossing occasionally, 20 to 30 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside.

In a large skillet, heat grapeseed oil over medium-high heat. Saute mushrooms and red onions with thyme sprigs, stirring frequently, until mushrooms are caramelized, about 7 minutes. Remove from heat, stir 4 tablespoons butter into hot mushrooms and discard thyme. Set mushrooms aside.

Use remaining butter to coat a 3-quart baking dish. In a large mixing bowl, whisk eggs, one cup cream and 2 cups chicken broth together. Add bread and stir until coated evenly. Fold in sweet potatoes, mushroom mixture and remaining herbs. If bread cubes seem dry, add more cream and chicken broth. Season with salt and pepper. Spoon stuffing into baking dish and bake until golden brown and cooked through, about 45 minutes.

ingredients.raw: 4 cinnamon sticks, each about 3 inches long
1 piece dried ginger root, 1 inch long
1 whole dried red pepper, 1 ½ inches long, chopped

steps.text: Wrap cinnamon sticks and ginger root in clean cloth.
Pound with mallet or hammer until finely crumbled; discard stringy parts of ginger. Add to remaining ingredients and stir well.
Store in airtight jars.
Use for pickling tongue, cucumbers, etc.

name: Mixed Red Fruit, Apricot and Hazelnut Galette
author: Martha Rose Shulman
description: In France, “fruits rouges” usually refers to a mixture of berries. I used blueberries and raspberries, and included some cherries and plums in the mix, as well as apricots for this delicious, rustic odds-and-ends galette.

ingredients.raw: 8 ounces (about 1 ½ cups) mixed berries or berries and cherries
ingredients.item: (about 1 ½ cups) mixed berries or berries and cherries

ingredients.raw: 1 pound mixed plums and apricots, pitted and quartered or sliced, depending on the size
ingredients.preparation: pitted and quartered or sliced, depending on the size

ingredients.raw: 30 grams (3 tablespoons) hazelnuts, lightly toasted, skinned and chopped (see below)
ingredients.preparation: lightly toasted, skinned and chopped (see below)

ingredients.raw: 1 egg beaten with 1 teaspoon milk, for egg wash

steps.text: Remove the pastry from the freezer and place it on a baking sheet lined with parchment. Leave it to thaw while you prepare the fruit, but don’t keep it out of the freezer for too long. It will thaw quickly, and it is easiest to handle if it's cold. You want it just soft enough so that you can manipulate it.
Combine the berries, apricots, plums, hazelnuts, almond extract and honey in a large bowl and gently toss together.

Sprinkle the almond powder over the pastry, leaving a 2- to 3-inch border all around. Place the fruit on top. Fold the edges of the dough in over the fruit, pleating the edges as you work your way around the fruit to form a free-form tart that is roughly 9 inches in diameter. Place in the freezer on the baking sheet for 45 minutes to an hour. This helps the galette maintain its shape.

Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 350 degrees. Remove the galette from the freezer. Brush the pastry with the egg wash. Combine the tablespoon of sugar and the ¼ teaspoon cinnamon and sprinkle over the fruit and the crust. Place in the oven and bake 1 hour, until the fruit is bubbly and the juice is running out and caramelizing on the parchment. Remove from the oven and allow to cool for at least 15 minutes. Serve hot or warm.

name: Mixed-Root-Vegetable Sauté
author: Mark Bittman
description: Each recipe below is based on a given root, but feel free to mess around. Bake beets instead of celeriac; make creamy potato soup, braise carrots, braise parsnips and so on.

steps.text: Cook a thinly sliced medium onion in olive oil over medium-high heat until tender, about 5 minutes.

Meanwhile, peel and grate a few carrots, sweet potatoes and radishes or turnips; add them, along with some minced garlic, to the pan and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, for another 5 minutes.
Add the juice of half a lime (this will loosen the mixture a bit), a sprinkle of chili powder, a handful of chopped scallions and fish sauce to taste
Garnish with lime wedges and serve.

ingredients.raw: 6 cups mixed salad greens like romaine, red-leaf lettuce, escarole, Boston, arugula, endive or frisee or mesclun
ingredients.preparation: red-leaf lettuce, escarole, Boston, arugula, endive or frisee or mesclun

ingredients.raw: Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

steps.text: Make sure you have enough different greens to provide a salad of varied texture and color. Wash and dry greens thoroughly in a salad spinner. Tear the leaves with your hands; if the leaves are small, use them whole.
In a large salad bowl, place mustard, vinegar, garlic, salt and pepper. Blend well.

Add the oil in a steady stream, whisking with a wire whisk until well blended. Since vinegar varies greatly in strength, taste to see if the vinaigrette has enough punch. Add more vinegar if necessary.
Add the greens, toss well with the vinaigrette and serve with the tuna.

ingredients.raw: 1 ¾ pounds spinach, stemmed and washed well
2 pounds mashing potatoes, peeled, halved lengthwise and cut crosswise into ¼-inch-thick slices
ingredients.preparation: peeled, halved lengthwise and cut crosswise into ¼-inch-thick slices

ingredients.raw: 12 medium carrots, peeled and cut crosswise into ¼-inch slices
ingredients.preparation: peeled and cut crosswise into ¼-inch slices

ingredients.raw: Freshly ground black pepper to taste
ingredients.item: freshly ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: In a tall stockpot, bring all the ingredients, except the salt, pepper and butter, to a boil. Lower the heat, and simmer for 30 minutes, or until each of the vegetables is easily pierced with the tip of a knife.

Pass the soup through the medium disk of a food mill, or skim the vegetables out of the liquid, and pulse them to a coarse puree in a food processor. If using a food processor, recombine the vegetables and the liquid. Season with salt and pepper. The soup may be refrigerated for up to 3 days or frozen for up to 2 months.
Bring to a simmer. If desired, stir a heaping ½ teaspoon of the butter into every portion just before serving.

ingredients.raw: 1 ½ cups green beans cut into 1 ½-inch lengths
ingredients.item: green beans cut into 1 ½-inch lengths

ingredients.raw: 1 ½ cups carrots cut into small batons ½-inch long
ingredients.item: carrots cut into small batons ½-inch long

ingredients.raw: 1 ½ cups small red potatoes, also cut into ½-inch batons
1 ½ cups white turnips cut into ½-inch batons
ingredients.item: white turnips cut into ½-inch batons

ingredients.raw: Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

ingredients.raw: 1 ½ cups zucchini cut into ½-inch batons

steps.text: In a heavy saucepan, heat the butter, and add the scallions. Cook briefly, then add the beans, carrots, potatoes, turnips, salt, pepper and water. Cover closely.
If the saucepan is heavy enough and the cover fits snugly, this should be sufficient water. Take care that the saucepan does not become dry or the vegetables will burn. Add more water if neccessary.

Cook over gentle to moderate heat for about 5 minutes, stirring and shaking the pan occasionally to redistribute the vegetables so they cook evenly. Then add the zucchini, cover the pan again, and cook for about 3 minutes more. Do not overcook.

Trim the beans and cut them into 1 ½-inch slices. Add them with the water and cook until they are tender and the water has evaporated (about 10 minutes). Scrape the kernels from the corn, add them to the skillet and cook for 3 minutes. Season with salt and pepper, sprinkle with basil and serve.

name: Miyan Masara (Corn Soup)
author: Yewande Komolafe
description: This recipe, from the chef Michael Elégbèdé, of the Lagos and New York-based dinner series Ìtàn, perfectly reflects his belief that ingredients are meant to evoke time and place. Across the vast Sahel and Savanna regions of West Africa, dried, ground or fermented masara (maize or corn in Hausa) is available year-round, but the fresh maize season (June to October) is an opportunity to partake in some of the region’s most exciting dishes: whole steamed and roasted cobs, maize dumplings, brothy vegetable soups. This soup celebrates corn in its simplest form. It begins with a cob-infused stock, then the kernels are lightly sautéed with onions, garlic and chile, as the stock is added and simmered. Maishanu, a type of clarified butter made from fresh cow milk, is a nod to the region’s nomadic, pastoral Fulani communities of the region, but the ghee here steps in. Proceed with caution when puréeing the hot soup to avoid any splatters, and add lime juice for a slight pop of acid. Mr. Elégbèdé recommends topping with crumbled goat cheese, fried crispy shallots, homemade or store-bought, and more ghee for a silky, full-bodied finish.

ingredients.raw: 3 medium carrots (about 6 ounces), roughly chopped (1 ½ cups)
2 tablespoons neutral oil, such as safflower, grapeseed or canola oil
ingredients.preparation: such as safflower, grapeseed or canola oil

ingredients.raw: 1 Scotch bonnet or habanero pepper, halved, seeds in or out
2 teaspoons kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal), more to taste
¼ cup roasted unsalted peanuts, roughly chopped
1 tablespoon fresh lime juice (from 1 fresh lime)
¼ cup plus 2 tablespoons maishanu or ghee
¼ cup crispy shallots, homemade or store-bought

steps.text: Prepare the stock: Shuck corn, reserving cobs. Using a paring knife, slice kernels into a medium bowl. Set aside.

Add corn cobs, onion, carrots, celery and cold water to a large stockpot over medium-high. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium to maintain a gentle simmer. Cook, uncovered, until vegetables are softened and liquid is three-fourths of the original volume, about 30 minutes. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve and discard solids. You should have about 4 cups stock.

Prepare the soup: Add oil to a large, heavy-bottomed pot and place over medium heat. Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and caramelized in spots, 10 to 12 minutes. Add garlic and Scotch bonnet, and cook until fragrant and softened, about 2 minutes. Add 1 teaspoon salt and reserved corn kernels, stirring to coat with onion mix. Cook until corn is bright yellow and warmed through, about 6 minutes.

Stir in remaining teaspoon salt and peanuts. Pour in all the prepared stock, increase heat to medium-high and bring to a simmer, about 6 minutes. Reduce heat to medium-low, and  simmer gently, stirring occasionally, until the liquid reduces by one-third, about 20 minutes.
In a small pot or saucepan over low heat, melt the maishanu, 1 to 2 minutes.

Working in batches, transfer the soup to a blender. Purée, beginning on low and gradually increasing the speed to high, until the soup is smooth, 4 minutes. (You can also use an immersion blender for this step.) With the motor running on low, stream in half of the melted maishanu. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve if a silky texture is desired, or leave as-is for a more rustic finish. Season to taste with lime juice, cayenne and more salt, if necessary.
To serve, ladle hot soup into warm bowls. Serve immediately, finishing with a drizzle of warm maishanu, a spoonful of crumbled goat cheese and a handful of crispy shallots.
